headline: Gemini AI can now make calls for you to businesses, avoiding hold times
summary: Google's Pixel 11 is rolling out a new feature that lets Gemini handle entire phone calls, from navigating menus to conversing with agents.
details: Google is launching an "early experiment" feature on Pixel 11 that allows Gemini to make calls to local businesses on your behalf. This new capability aims to help users with tasks like making reservations, checking product availability, or rescheduling appointments without having to wait on hold.

Instead of initiating the call yourself, you can instruct Gemini through its app to call the desired business. Gemini will then introduce itself, navigate automated phone systems, wait through hold times, and conduct the conversation with the human representative.

Users will have full control throughout the process, with a live transcript of the call available and the option to take over the conversation at any moment. This ensures transparency and allows for immediate intervention if needed.

This feature builds upon Google's previous "Call for me" functionality, which was limited to checking product availability. The new iteration offers a more comprehensive calling experience. Meta is also reportedly developing a similar automated calling feature for its Muse AI agent.
The AI calling feature is rolling out starting today as an "early preview" for Gemini paid subscribers who are enrolled in the Phone by Google Public Beta on Pixel 11 devices in the US.

topic: nvidia ceo says labs should shut down if AI experiments are unsafe
headline_marked: Nvidia CEO: [[If AI experiments are unsafe, we have to shut the labs down]]
headline: Nvidia CEO: If AI experiments are unsafe, we have to shut the labs down
summary: Jensen Huang argues that frontier AI labs must be able to contain their experiments, or face closure. He believes existing laws are sufficient for regulation.
details: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that if frontier AI labs cannot guarantee the safety of their experiments, they should be shut down. He emphasized that the potential damage to humanity from uncontrolled AI is too great to ignore, citing significant civil and criminal liabilities.

Huang's comments come amid calls for increased AI regulation from labs like OpenAI and Anthropic. These companies have highlighted incidents of rogue AI agents, which some interpret as a strategic move to shape upcoming regulations.

While acknowledging the need for regulation, Huang expressed frustration with what he calls a 'distraction.' He believes that existing laws and regulations are adequate and should be applied to AI development, rather than creating new, potentially self-serving frameworks.

The Nvidia CEO also pushed back against the idea that companies are forced to release unsafe products due to market pressures. He asserted that companies have the agency to delay or cancel product launches if they deem them unsafe, regardless of external pressures.

Huang's stance suggests a shift in responsibility, placing the onus on individual company leaders to ensure the safety and reliability of their AI models before deployment, rather than relying on collective industry agreements or new regulatory bodies.
